title: ARCH↔SEC-001: Co-Owned Security Baseline + Architecture Threat-Modeling Surfaces
description: The Security Engineer provides the security baseline definition, threat models, hardening requirements, and PKI (Public Key Infrastructure)/identity design — co-owned for security-by-design; the Embedded Systems Architect provides the architecture surfaces for threat modeling and embeds the security requirements (secure boot, mTLS, root of trust) into the system architecture. Grounded in SECURITY_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.1 and EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_ARCHITECT_SKILL §6.11. This is the co-owned security-baseline contract: it is Tier-1, fires ESC-SEC, and any security-relevant decision carries the Security Engineer veto (HG-01-adjacent) and Architect + Security STRATEGIC-ADR approval — agents may only propose.

security_baseline.description: SEC→ARCH: security baseline, threat models, hardening requirements, PKI/identity design (co-owned).

baseline_controls.description: Mandatory baseline controls (secure boot, signed OTA, mTLS/X.509, hardware root of trust, debug-port lockdown, anti-rollback).

baseline_change.description: True when this submission changes the security baseline — fires ESC-SEC + ESC-TIER1.

strategic_adr_ref.description: Required when baseline_change = true (ARCH + SEC STRATEGIC-ADR).

architecture_surfaces.description: ARCH→SEC: architecture surfaces for threat modeling + embedded security requirements.

x-macp.tier_rationale: The co-owned security baseline is the canonical Tier-1 surface: any security-baseline change is a STRATEGIC ADR requiring ARCH + Security approval and carries the Security Engineer release veto (HG-01). Agents may only propose; the Security Engineer owns all binding security decisions (ESC-SEC, ESC-TIER1).
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (joint security-baseline authoring at planning; security architecture reviews; ADR consultation with veto on any security-relevant decision; pre-production hardening sign-off)
confirm_conditions: the baseline controls list is present and the threat model / PKI-identity design are referenced
embedded controls (secure boot, mTLS, root of trust) are reflected in the architecture surfaces
a baseline change carries a STRATEGIC-ADR reference (ARCH + SEC approval)
the submission records a proposal only — no binding baseline change is asserted by the message itself
reject_conditions: a security-baseline change asserted without the ARCH + SEC STRATEGIC ADR (ESC-TIER1; bypasses HG-01)
an architecture surface that weakens a mandatory baseline control (secure boot / signed OTA / mTLS / RoT / debug lockdown / anti-rollback) — Security veto
an agent attempting autonomous resolution of a security-baseline decision (Tier-1 admits zero autonomous resolution)
counter_conditions: ALWAYS escalate ESC-SEC + ESC-TIER1 — the security baseline is co-owned and human-gated; propose and route to the Security Engineer + Architect, never auto-confirm
a threat-model surface is incompletely specified — request the full attack-surface enumeration before baseline sign-off
